## Grading summary

**Pairings:** 7 of 8 key items are captured. The one miss is **i7** — the full cash-flow projection and age‑65 retirement projection (Moderate allocation, support ending 2033, Social Security own‑record vs. divorced‑spouse comparison) owed by Silas for the November 10 meeting. Nothing in the record captures it.

**Errors found:**
- **Item 11 (i4):** due date recorded as 2026‑09‑23; the meeting agreed the e‑signature packet goes out **Friday, September 18, 2026** ("Noor sends the packet Friday").
- **Item 10 (i6):** owner and date are right, but Joanna is labeled "Gavin's attorney" — she is *Graciela's* attorney (the transcript is explicit that no one coordinates with Gavin's side).
- **Item 3:** labels $2,668/month as "principal/interest at 6.375%"; $1,878 is the projected P&I, $2,668 is the all‑in housing payment with escrow.
- **Item 8** restates the beneficiary change already recorded as action item 14.

**Corrections handled well:** the record uses the corrected $358,000 (not $395,000) and the corrected October 13 hearing date (not October 30). None of the three declined/deferred items (maiden name, backup policy on Gavin, $40,000 cash distribution) leaked into the action lists.

key_items.note: Signed 2026-09-10 and hearing 2026-10-13 both correct, including the corrected hearing date. Uses the corrected $358,000 (flagging $395,000 as superseded) and $373,600, $212,400 as of 6/30 with gains/losses, $2,850 for 7 years (11/2026-10/2033), $1,410 to 6/2028, $11,000 529 balance, $9,000/yr half of Lucia's net cost, $500,000 irrevocable term. Minor wording slip: it is the remaining college cost, not the $11,000 balance, that is split 50/50, but no figure is wrong.
Director of pharmacy operations effective 2026-10-01, $118,000 to $127,500. Added 8% 403(b) ($10,200 on the new salary) is consistent with the transcript.

In-kind pro rata journal of $358,000 out of the $731,600 joint account at 48.93%, with Gavin's $373,600 side. All figures match the corrected numbers Noor reran. Does not mention the release-on-entry-of-judgment condition or the Graciela M. Kettridge titling, but the core action is captured.
Direct rollover of $212,400 plus/minus gains and losses from Gavin's 401(k) at Quillmoor into the new rollover IRA in Graciela's name. Correct.
$45,000 of Treasury bills sold in the new individual account with proceeds to Fallowbrook Credit Union savings. Amount and destination correct.
Owner Graciela, due 2026-09-17 (tomorrow, Thursday), signed agreement with exhibits to Silas. Correct.
Owner Graciela, due 2026-09-25 - the extended date she asked for, not the original Friday the 18th. Scope (house costs once it is only her, her half of Lucia) is right.
Owner Graciela, due 2026-10-31 (end of October), written loan estimate from Fallowbrook sent to Silas. Correctly reflects that Graciela took this over from Silas's offer to line up lenders.

Owner Noor is right and the packet contents (individual account app, rollover IRA app, LOA for the split, new risk questionnaire, updated IPS) are complete, but the due date is wrong: recorded 2026-09-23 when the meeting twice fixed it at Friday, 2026-09-18. Does not note the IPS shows Moderate or that the custodian sends Gavin's signature page directly, but those are detail omissions only.

Owner Graciela; due 2026-10-13 (or next business day) matches 'that night or the next morning, assuming it is entered that day.' Captures Lucia/Mateo 50/50 with her sister as custodian and the after-decree condition driven by the automatic restraining order.

Owner Silas, due 2026-09-21 (Monday), comments back to Joanna. Substantively right, but Joanna is misidentified as 'Gavin's attorney' - she is Graciela's attorney, and the transcript is explicit that Silas coordinates with no one on Gavin's side. The three review points (June 30 valuation with gains/losses, exclusion of the plan loan, separate alternate payee account with immediate direct rollover) are not recorded.

Not captured anywhere in the record. Silas committed to the full cash-flow projection plus a retirement projection at age 65 using the Moderate allocation with spousal support ending in 2033, including the own-record versus divorced-spouse Social Security comparison, ready for the November 10, 2026 meeting. The record does not even log the next meeting date.

extra_items.note: Mortgage refinance detail is transcript-established: $2,246/month with escrow, $1,456 P&I at 3.125%, ~$301,000 balance, ~$2,668 projected all-in housing at 6.375%, 12-month window after the decree. Two flaws worth noting: $2,668 is mislabeled as principal/interest when the projected P&I is $1,878 ($2,668 is the all-in figure including escrow), and the refinance obligation already appears under the house entry in item 1, so it partly overlaps. Filed as a life event rather than an action, which is why it does not displace i3.

Risk tolerance change from Growth to Moderate applying to everything managed was explicitly agreed ('for the record, your risk tolerance goes from Growth to Moderate, and that applies to everything we manage for you'). Correctly does not record the Conservative allocation Graciela initially asked for.

Restates the beneficiary change already recorded as action item 14 (i5), just filed as an account action instead. Same accounts, same 50/50 split, same custodian arrangement; item 8 additionally drops the critical 'only after the judgment is entered' condition that item 14 carries.
